body: Should this be possible? As we don't expose `setIndex`, I feel like this test isn't needed
it should be calling `getWidgetRenderState().refine` for an equivalent test
however it makes sense that this is tested in the connector alone
we probably prefer throwing instead of setting to an empty string, or even `if initialIndex setIndex`
Wouldn't it be a breaking change? For now, we accept it to be `undefined` if I understand correctly

in the previous implementation setIndex was called with undefined, which I think would already not be the behaviour you want (it would make subsequent calls fail):

```

> const helper = require('algoliasearch-helper')
undefined
> const h = helper({search: console.log}, 'test')
undefined
> h.search()
[ { indexName: 'test', params: { facets: [], tagFilters: '' } } ]
> h.setIndex().search()
[ { indexName: undefined, params: { facets: [], tagFilters: '' } } ]
```

I'm in favour of either keeping it broken in the same was as before (`initialIndex!`), or only calling setIndex if we know the previous index, otherwise leaving it as-is (plus adding a new test for that behaviour preferably)


I'm not sure if it's even possible to call dispose before getWidgetRenderState is ever called though, so this is definitely an edge case!
Warns and only call `setIndex` when the previous index is defined: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4700/commits/f725991120710cd96605fc8a9c0db9fd1d04a3ea
I don't think this really needs a warning, since there's no practical way of it happening :)
Should it need a test then? As it can't really happen
